classification.difficultyReason: Apply a supplied multistep procedure to chosen starting values to generate Pythagorean triples.

content.prompt:
Produce some more Pythagorean triples using this method, starting with some other odd numbers.

Take an odd number as the length of one side. Square it and subtract 1. Halve the result to obtain the second side, then add 1 to obtain the hypotenuse.

answer.worked:
Sample answers:

Starting with $3$:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Second side}&=\frac{3^2-1}{2}\\\text{Second side}&=4\\\text{Hypotenuse}&=4+1=5\end{align*}$$
The triple is $(3,4,5)$.

Starting with $5$:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Second side}&=\frac{5^2-1}{2}\\\text{Second side}&=12\\\text{Hypotenuse}&=12+1=13\end{align*}$$
The triple is $(5,12,13)$.

Starting with $7$:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Second side}&=\frac{7^2-1}{2}\\\text{Second side}&=24\\\text{Hypotenuse}&=24+1=25\end{align*}$$
The triple is $(7,24,25)$.
